subject.title: [Bug]: OpenAI provider fails with "Invalid value: 'custom'" – tool parameter incompatibility

question: For API-key-backed `openai/*` embedded agent turns, should OpenClaw normalize unsupported custom tool descriptors before entering the native Codex app-server path, or select a documented direct/PI OpenAI runtime when that payload shape is required?
rationale: The documentation makes the native Codex app-server the default embedded OpenAI runtime, while the closed proposals only reject a downstream Responses tool choice; maintainers need to choose the durable ownership boundary before a repair changes runtime routing or tool semantics.

options.title: Normalize at the owning request boundary
options.body: Recommended: preserve the existing native embedded runtime and convert or reject invalid descriptors where OpenClaw first projects tools for OpenAI, with regression coverage for every downstream transport.

options.title: Route API-key embedded turns explicitly
options.body: Define a supported direct or PI runtime selection for API-key-backed embedded OpenAI turns and document the compatibility trade-off.

options.title: Require a new current-main trace first
options.body: Pause implementation until a maintainer or reporter supplies a redacted current-main request trace proving which payload producer still emits the unsupported value.

recommendation.title: Normalize at the owning request boundary
recommendation.body: Recommended: preserve the existing native embedded runtime and convert or reject invalid descriptors where OpenClaw first projects tools for OpenAI, with regression coverage for every downstream transport.

likelyOwner.reason: The available related history most directly connects this person to the Codex app-server runtime boundary that current documentation identifies for embedded OpenAI turns.
